questions.text: Tensile (normal) stress acts ___ to the plane of the surface.
questions.explanation: Normal (tensile) stress acts perpendicular to the surface.

questions.text: Shear stress acts ___ to the plane of the surface.
questions.explanation: Shear stress acts parallel (tangentially) to the surface.

questions.text: Pressure is defined as the ___.
options: force acting perpendicularly per unit area
questions.explanation: Pressure = perpendicular force per unit area.

questions.text: The SI unit of pressure is the ___.
questions.explanation: Pa = N/m² (one newton per square metre).

questions.text: The hydrostatic pressure at a depth h in a liquid of density ρ is given by ___.
questions.explanation: P = ρgh.

questions.text: In a liquid at rest, the pressure ___ with depth.
questions.explanation: Pressure in a liquid increases with depth.

questions.text: The relative density of a substance is the ratio of its density to the density of ___.
questions.explanation: Relative density is measured against the density of water.

questions.text: Archimedes' principle states that the upthrust on a body immersed in a fluid is equal to ___.
options: the weight of the fluid displaced by the body
questions.explanation: Upthrust equals the weight of the fluid displaced.

questions.text: A body floats in a liquid when the buoyant force is ___.
options: greater than or equal to its weight
questions.explanation: The body floats when buoyancy is at least as large as its weight.

questions.text: A body sinks in a liquid when its ___.
options: weight is greater than the buoyant force
weight is less than the buoyant force
questions.explanation: The body sinks when mg > buoyant force.

questions.text: In laminar (streamline) flow, the fluid moves ___.
options: smoothly in parallel layers without intermixing
questions.explanation: Laminar flow is smooth parallel-layer flow below the critical velocity.

questions.text: Turbulent flow occurs when the velocity of a fluid ___.
questions.explanation: Above the critical velocity the flow becomes turbulent.

questions.text: For a Reynolds number Re less than 2000, the flow is ___.
questions.explanation: Re < 2000 gives laminar flow.

questions.text: For a Reynolds number Re greater than 4000, the flow is ___.
questions.explanation: Re > 4000 gives turbulent flow.

questions.text: Viscosity is a measure of a fluid's ___.
questions.explanation: Viscosity measures the fluid's resistance to flow.

questions.text: When the temperature of a liquid increases, its viscosity ___.
questions.explanation: Viscosity decreases as temperature increases.

questions.text: Stokes' law gives the viscous drag on a sphere of radius r moving with velocity v in a fluid of viscosity η as ___.
questions.explanation: F = 6πηrv.

questions.text: At terminal velocity, the acceleration of a falling sphere through a viscous liquid is ___.
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity the net force is zero, so a = 0.

questions.text: Terminal velocity is reached when the viscous drag on the falling body just balances the ___.
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity, viscous drag balances weight and upthrust.

questions.text: Surface tension is the force acting ___ per unit length of an imaginary line drawn on the liquid surface.
questions.explanation: Surface tension acts tangentially to the liquid surface.

questions.text: The SI unit of surface tension is ___.
questions.explanation: Surface tension = force per unit length, measured in N/m.

questions.text: The surface of a liquid behaves like ___.
questions.explanation: Surface tension makes the liquid surface act like a stretched elastic skin.

questions.text: Surface tension of a liquid ___ when its temperature increases.
questions.explanation: Heating weakens the intermolecular forces, lowering surface tension.

questions.text: Adding soap or detergent to water ___ its surface tension.
questions.explanation: Soap (an impurity) lowers the surface tension of water.

questions.text: The excess pressure inside a liquid drop of surface tension γ and radius r is ___.
questions.explanation: A liquid drop has one surface, so excess pressure = 2γ/r.

questions.text: Because a soap bubble has two liquid surfaces, its excess pressure is ___.
questions.explanation: A soap bubble has two surfaces, giving excess pressure = 4γ/r.

questions.text: Adhesion is the force of attraction between molecules of ___.
questions.explanation: Adhesion acts between unlike substances, e.g. water and glass.

questions.text: Cohesion is the force of attraction between molecules of ___.
questions.explanation: Cohesion acts between identical molecules.

questions.text: Water rises in a narrow glass capillary tube mainly because of the ___.
options: adhesive force between water and glass
questions.explanation: Capillary rise is due to adhesion between water and glass.

questions.text: Water rises 2 cm in a capillary tube of radius r. In a tube of radius r/3, the same water will rise to ___.
questions.explanation: hr is constant, so h₂ = 3 × 2 = 6 cm.

questions.text: Most solids and liquids ___ when their temperature is increased.
questions.explanation: Heating increases molecular vibration, so solids and liquids expand.

questions.text: The increase in length of a solid rod on heating is given by ___.
questions.explanation: ΔL = αLiΔT.

questions.text: The coefficient of linear expansion α is measured in ___.
questions.explanation: The unit of α is 1/°C.

questions.text: The coefficient of area (superficial) expansion of a solid is related to its linear expansivity α by ___.
questions.explanation: Area expansivity = 2α.

questions.text: The coefficient of volume (cubic) expansion of a solid is related to its linear expansivity α by ___.
questions.explanation: Cubic expansivity = 3α.

questions.text: The increase in volume of a liquid on heating is given by ___.
questions.explanation: ΔV = βViΔT.

questions.text: A brass rod 3 cm long at 0°C (α = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵/°C) is heated to 100°C. Its increase in length is ___.
10 litres of mercury (β = 1.8 × 10⁻⁴/°C) is heated through 30°C. Its increase in volume is ___.
A bimetallic strip is commonly used in a ___.
questions.explanation: Bimetallic strips are used in thermostats.

questions.text: Gaps are left between railway rails mainly to ___.
options: allow for the contraction of trains
allow for the expansion of the rails when heated
questions.explanation: The gaps accommodate thermal expansion of the rails.

questions.text: Heat is best described as ___.
options: thermal energy in transit from a hotter body to a colder body
the total kinetic energy of a body
the internal energy stored in a body
questions.explanation: Heat is thermal energy in transit due to a temperature difference.

questions.text: Heat always flows from the body at ___.
options: lower temperature to the body at higher temperature
the same temperature to a colder one
higher temperature to the body at lower temperature
questions.explanation: Heat flows from hot to cold.

questions.text: The SI unit of heat is the ___.
questions.explanation: Heat is measured in joules (J).

questions.text: 1 calorie is approximately equal to ___.
Temperature is a measure of the ___ of a body.
questions.explanation: Temperature measures hotness or coldness.

questions.text: The zeroth law of thermodynamics states that if A and B are each in thermal equilibrium with C, then ___.
options: A and B cannot be in equilibrium
A and B are in thermal equilibrium with each other
heat flows from A to B
questions.explanation: Thermal equilibrium is transitive by the zeroth law.

questions.text: On the Celsius scale, the lower fixed point is ___.
questions.explanation: The ice point is 0°C.

questions.text: On the Fahrenheit scale, the upper fixed point is ___.
questions.explanation: The steam point is 212°F.

questions.text: The fundamental interval on the Fahrenheit scale is ___.
The SI unit of thermodynamic temperature is the ___.
questions.explanation: Kelvin (K) is the SI unit of temperature.

questions.text: A temperature of 20°C is equal to about ___.
A temperature of 50°C is equal to ___ on the Fahrenheit scale.
Absolute zero (0 K) is equal to about ___.
The triple point of water is defined as ___.
questions.explanation: The triple point of water is 273.16 K.

questions.text: Latent heat of fusion is the heat required to change ___ at constant temperature.
questions.explanation: Fusion is the solid-to-liquid change.

questions.text: Latent heat of vaporization is the heat required to change ___ at constant temperature.
questions.explanation: Vaporization is the liquid-to-vapour change.

questions.text: During melting or boiling of a pure substance, its temperature ___.
questions.explanation: Temperature stays constant during a change of state.

questions.text: The main mode of heat transfer in solids is ___.
questions.explanation: Conduction is the main mode of heat transfer in solids.

questions.text: The main mode of heat transfer in fluids (liquids and gases) is ___.
questions.explanation: Convection by moving fluid particles dominates in fluids.

questions.text: Heat from the sun reaches the earth by ___.
questions.explanation: Radiant heat travels through space at the speed of light.
